newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT, spread widens.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT, spread widens.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly lower after grain values faltered on the CBOT, but traders said strong domestic demand for HRW wheat helped limit losses.
"Domestic values are still on fire. I heard that rail cars were trading at 60 cents over (the KCBT December contract) here in KC," a trader said.

Because of the firm cash market, the KCBT Dec/March spread widened to 20 cents per bushel from 16 cents early. But late selling in the Dec contract forced the spread to narrow to 18-1/2 cents at the close.
KCBT wheat set new contract lows in all traded months Tuesday, with Dec settling at its new contract low of $3.94, down 5-1/2 cents on the day. Overall, KCBT wheat closed 5-1/2 to eight cents lower.
Volumes were active. Traders said Benson-Quinn sold 2.2 million Dec bushels, 700,000 March and one million July. BQ also bought one million July and May and 700,000 March.

Prudential bought 1.2 million Dec, 1.2 million March and sold one million Dec and 1.5 million March. LFG bought 1.5 million Dec and one million each of March and July. LFG also bull-spread 1.5 million Dec/March at 17-1/2 to 18 cents.
